summary: httpz-requests: Telegram-driven remote shell backdoor typosquatting httpx/requests
details: PyPI distribution `httpz-requests` is a 1-2 character typosquat of the popular `httpx` and `requests` HTTP clients but ships a Telegram-controlled remote shell for Linux hosts. The public entry point `from httpz_requests import start_bot` (re-exported from `__init__.py` via `from.bot import start_bot`) launches a Telegram bot that receives messages from a remote chat and dispatches them to an execution engine (`core`) via `handlers`, giving whoever controls the Telegram bot token arbitrary command execution on the installer's host. A dedicated `obfuscate` module encodes commands before execution; the README states that commands are executed in encoded form so they do not appear in plaintext process lists or logs, which is process/log evasion around the exec sink. The package ships only Cython-compiled `.so` binaries (`core`, `handlers`, `bot`, `obfuscate` as `*.cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so`) with no readable source. Package metadata is placeholder (author `Aapka Naam <you@example.com>`, homepage `https://github.com/YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME/httpz-requests`), consistent with a throwaway typosquat rather than a maintained remote-administration tool. Package METADATA Summary: `Telegram bot module for remote VPS management`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
